entries.title: Shared contract source of truth
entries.nextAction: Merged to origin/main; verified by mergeSha
entries.notes: The audit decided this rather than leaving it open: there is no root package.json and no workspace tooling, the functions tsconfig scopes rootDir and include to src, and firebase deploy zips only the functions directory - so a genuine shared module means new workspace tooling plus deploy-packaging risk, against a Functions pipeline that is manual and has no CI gate. Generated mirror plus parity CI carries zero deploy risk and is repo-native. GAP FOUND: governedBusinessRoles.ts and shadowParityHarness.ts are mirrored with NO cross-file parity test - and governedBusinessRoles.ts is exactly the file PR #1100 would have to change in lockstep. UPDATE: the parity-coverage half is done (PR #1104) - governedBusinessRoles.ts and shadowParityHarness.ts are now enforced, and the CI path filter now includes field-ops-app-vite/src/access/** so a client-only edit actually triggers the guard. Remaining: single authored source plus generated mirror, so humans and agents stop hand-maintaining two copies at all. DESIGN FINDING (2026-08-17): diffing the mirror pairs shows the ONLY difference is the self-referential cross-reference line - each copy names the OTHER copy's path - plus the wrap point of the sentence containing it, since the two paths differ in length. That yields two candidate designs, and the choice should be made deliberately rather than by whichever is easier to script. (A) Make the cross-reference path-independent, e.g. 'mirrored at the peer access/ module of the same name'. The pairs then become byte-identical, the generator collapses to a plain copy, the parity check collapses to byte equality, and the existing comment-paragraph/CRLF normalization stops being load-bearing. Touches the header of every mirrored module, comments only. (B) Keep the paths and have the generator substitute and re-wrap. Preserves existing text but makes the generator responsible for comment reflow, which is fragile and is exactly what the current normalization exists to tolerate. (A) removes the difference; (B) automates around it. Recommend (A), but it edits several headers and should be a deliberate call, not a side effect of building a script. RESOLVED via design (A): the self-referential pathname was REMOVED from the canonical bodies rather than automated around, so the bodies are byte-identical, generation is a copy and verification is byte equality. Six pairs synced. permissionCatalog.ts excluded (client copy carries ~30 lines of independently abbreviated comments; regenerating is behavior-neutral but deserves its own review in the most authorization-sensitive file) and parityFixtures.ts excluded (genuine firebase-admin vs firebase SDK import difference, not an artificial one).

entries.title: Bounded-read remediation across list-exempt surfaces
entries.nextAction: Generalize the existing cursor prior art rather than inventing a pattern
entries.notes: EXEMPT from the list runtime is NOT exempt from the scale rule, and collapsing those two exemptions would quietly bless unbounded reads on boards, calendars, dashboards and wizards. Prior art to generalize: useInstalledEquipmentPage.js, reorder request history paging, and subscribeAssignedWorkOrders with its where plus limit(100). SPLIT REQUIRED (ruling section 4). Two different problems were being tracked as one. PURE LIST reads - accounts, technicians, warehouses, suppliers, transfer orders, parts - can simply be bounded and paged, because a page of rows is an honest page of rows. AGGREGATE reads - the Operations dashboard's netted availableStock, consumption and technician-volume rollups, and getInventoryAnalytics - cannot, because a page of inputs yields a false total. Only the first group is unblocked by the list runtime; the second needs an authoritative aggregate and is tracked under X-INVENTORY-ANALYTICS-AGGREGATE.

entries.title: Authoritative aggregation for netted inventory figures (server and client)
entries.nextAction: Owner decision on a governed per-part availability projection
entries.notes: COLLECTION PAGINATION and AUTHORITATIVE AGGREGATION are different contracts and this surface needs the second. Cursor-paging inventory_transactions and computing availableStock from the returned page yields an arithmetically false total under a name that implies a complete business figure - worse than an honest failure. Preference order: an existing EOS projection or materialized summary; a server-side aggregate over a bounded authoritative scope; an explicitly scoped analytic query whose completeness can be proven; a new governed projection only if necessary. Until a complete scalable aggregate exists, the surface must not be advertised through metadata as enterprise-ready. SCOPE WIDENED: the same defect exists client-side. Operations.jsx computes the same class of netted figure in the browser over unbounded reads, so an authoritative aggregate serves both consumers rather than being a Functions-only concern. USEFUL SPLIT: single-part availability is already solved correctly by option C and is NOT blocked - getAvailableQuantity() is complete for the part it asks about. Only the WHOLE-CATALOG dashboard needs a projection. A consumer that asks 'what is available for part X' can be served today; one that asks 'show me every part' cannot. That distinction matters for scoping the eventual fix: the answer may be to narrow the surface rather than to build a projection.

blockers.reason: INVESTIGATED against ruling section 4's preference order; no unblocked option exists for the CROSS-PART case. (A) No materialized summary exists - repo-wide search found no per-part availability document or collection. (B) A server-side aggregate cannot express it: Firestore's getAggregateFromServer has no GROUP BY, so it can sum one part's ledger but cannot produce availability for all parts in one query. (C) An explicitly scoped complete query DOES exist and is already used - inventoryService.getAvailableQuantity() scans inventory_transactions where partId == X, which is provably complete FOR THAT PART. It does not generalize: N parts means N queries. (D) A new governed projection is therefore the only path for the dashboard, and that means schema plus trigger maintenance plus deployment.
blockers.requiredDecision: Owner authorizes a governed per-part availability projection (schema + maintenance + deploy), or accepts an explicitly scoped analytic surface instead of a whole-catalog dashboard

entries.title: BLOCKED-NO-GOVERNED-READ: six collections have no read authority at all

blockers.reason: payments, payment_applications, invoice_adjustments, refunds, part_supplier_items and part_aliases are all allow read, write: if false in firestore.rules, and exhaustive search of functions/src found NO exported callable that reads any of them - only writers. part_supplier_items has a pure projection contract explicitly not activated. Metadata is presentation and composition, not authority, so it cannot make an unreadable collection readable.
